evidence.trustReason: Fresh-context review of packages/opencode/test/task/verify-spec-RM3.spec.ts (4 tests, my own run: 4 pass, 0 fail, 99 expect calls, 5.5 s). Given/When (engine module inspected): the test imports the runtime exports of engine-xstate/index.ts, machine.ts, alphabet.ts and core/events.ts and reads their source with comments blanked out; it pins the engine file set to exactly those four files. Then (no obligation, task, scenario or run machine beside the generated one): no module exports obligationMachine, taskMachine, scenarioMachine or runMachine, and no exported value is a machine; the only createMachine/setup call in the engine module is fromConfig's createMachine(check(plan, built)), which machine(plan) calls; none of the four names is an identifier anywhere in src; initial(plan).machine and a TaskEvents.fold of the observed facts both belong to machine(plan) and hold no child actor. And (no stepTask, stepRun, cancel, staleAlone or follows code): none of these names (nor stepObligation, stepScenario, runSnapshot) is an identifier in the engine module; all but cancel are absent from all of src (cancel remains only as supervision job code outside the engine module, which the Given scopes out; I confirmed the only engine 'cancel' word is a comment). A control proves the scanner finds each name in the old module's shape and ignores comments and longer names. And (XStateEngine keeps name, initial and apply over an opaque snapshot): keys are exactly name, initial, apply; name is 'xstate' as before (old index.ts:890); arities 1 and 3; the source types them over RunSnapshot = SnapshotFrom<RunMachine>; no engine function takes a State; at run time the snapshot has none of the old State fields, apply keeps the same machine, and callers read it through view and the selectors. Real modules, no mocks.
